newsitem.title: GERMANY: German interior minister opposes immigration bill.
newsitem.headline: German interior minister opposes immigration bill.

text.p: Interior Minister Manfred Kanther on Saturday rejected calls from members of Germany's ruling coalition for an immigration law setting quotas on the number of foreigners allowed into the country.
"Germany's capacity to take in foreigners through immigration policy is already exhausted. We don't require immigration now or in the next few years," Kanther said.

The liberal Free Democrats (FDP), junior partners in Chancellor Helmut Kohl's coalition, said this week they would present a bill which would allow a set number of foreigners into Germany each year according to the country's needs.
The FDP's bill is also likely to extend citizenship automatically to many foreigners born in Germany. The current rules for citizenship rely overwhelmingly on blood lines.
Kanther's comments, released by the Bild am Sonntag newspaper ahead of publication on Sunday, indicated that the draft law faces stiff resistance from within the coalition.

"We already have more than seven million foreigners and we have 4.7 million unemployed, who find it more and more difficult to get into the jobs market, and there are half a million foreigners among them," Kanther said.

Under the FDP's plans, Germany would select immigrants according to its needs, giving preference to people who could do particular jobs or who were from a certain age group. Kanther said the plans were too vague.
"No one has convincingly answered the question of which criteria would be applied in the selection process," he said.

Officially, Germany does not accept immigration by foreigners from outside the European Union. But every year it takes in tens of thousands of asylum seekers, and people of German descent from former Soviet republics and eastern Europe.
